svg.title: Prometheus & Grafana
svg.desc: Prometheus & Grafana. Pull-based monitoring: scrape metrics into a time-series database, query them with PromQL, alert, and chart them in Grafana. Step 1, Where it sits: Prometheus pulls /metrics every 15 s, stores samples, alerts via Alertmanager and serves Grafana. Step 2, Scrape and store: Each /metrics line is one sample of one series: into the head and WAL, then 2-hour blocks on disk. Step 3, Query and alert: rate() turns counters into rates. 6% errors for 10 min fires the alert; Alertmanager pages on-call. Step 4, Limits and trade-offs: Each label value is a series in memory; one server keeps 15 days locally; remote_write keeps more.

g.text: Prometheus pulls /metrics every 15 s, stores samples, alerts via Alertmanager and serves Grafana.
Each /metrics line is one sample of one series: into the head and WAL, then 2-hour blocks on disk.
rate() turns counters into rates. 6% errors for 10 min fires the alert; Alertmanager pages on-call.
Each label value is a series in memory; one server keeps 15 days locally; remote_write keeps more.
one server is not HA: run two, Alertmanager dedupes
row = one series · square = one sample
Service discovery finds the targets through the Kubernetes API, and the scraper fetches /metrics from each one every 15 s (default 1 min).
Samples go into the local TSDB; rules run on them every 15 s, firing alerts go to Alertmanager, and Grafana reads the same data with PromQL.
ONE LINE, ONE SAMPLE, ONE SERIES
http_requests_total{service="catalog",status="200"} 18420 from catalog-7d9, plus job, instance and pod = one series.
Samples go to the in-memory head and its write-ahead log. Every 2 h the oldest 2 h of the head become a block on disk; 3 × 2h compact to 6h.
rate() makes per-second rates and absorbs counter resets. Above 5% the alert is pending; after 10 min it fires, and on-call is paged.
Every label value is a new series in memory: user_id on 12 series makes up to 600,000. Local data stays 15 days, on one server.
metrics are aggregates: per-request detail is in logs and traces
